sections.h2: Who sets and collects property tax in Wyoming?
sections.html:
The county assessor values property, local governments set the mill levies, and the county treasurer collects the money. The state Department of Revenue Property Tax Division trains and supports the local offices and assesses public utility property such as pipelines, railroads and telecommunications. Residential tax is never paid to the division, so send payments to your county treasurer.

The Legislature sets the assessment ratio. Residential property is assessed at 9.5 percent of market value, industrial property at 11.5 percent and minerals at 100 percent of fair market value. School districts, hospital districts, towns and counties then levy the mills they need to fund their budgets.

For a seller, this means your valuation comes from one office, your rate from several taxing districts, and your bill from a third. When a number looks wrong, the assessor handles value questions and the treasurer handles payment questions.

sections.h2: How a Wyoming property tax bill is calculated
sections.html:
The formula is market value times the assessment ratio times the mill levy, divided by 1,000. One mill equals $1 per $1,000 of assessed value.

The statewide average mill levy for 2025 was 65.280. County averages ran from 57.772 in Teton County, the lowest, to 73.826 in Big Horn County, the highest. Natrona County averaged 72.238 mills and Weston County 73.210. Two houses of equal value can carry noticeably different yearly bills depending on which taxing districts they sit in, and a buyer will look at that number.

Residential property makes up about 30 percent of total assessed value in Wyoming, and minerals about 44 percent. Your own levy is printed on the bill from the county treasurer.

The 25 percent exemption, created by Senate Enrolled Act 60 in 2025, cuts the taxable value of a home by 25 percent on fair market value up to $1 million. It has no expiration date, and the bill carried no backfill money for special districts, local governments or schools that lose revenue.

It covers owner-occupied houses, condominiums, townhouses and manufactured homes where the owner lives at least eight months a year. Some military members who cannot meet the eight-month rule may still qualify. Owners file an affidavit with the county assessor. The deadline in the second year moved to March 1 from February 1 when the Department of Revenue extended it, so ask the assessor for the current filing date. Homeowners using the long-term homeowners exemption do not qualify for the 25 percent reduction until tax year 2027.

Besides the 25 percent exemption, Wyoming has a refund program, a veteran exemption and a senior reduction. Each has its own application and its own office, so check which ones a seller already has on file.

  • Property tax refund: for homeowners who struggle to pay. Households at or below 125 percent of county median income receive 75 percent of taxes paid, capped at half the county's median residential bill. The ceiling is 145 percent of county median income, and those between 126 and 145 percent receive that amount reduced by 35 percent.
  • Veteran exemption: rose from $3,000 to $6,000 in 2024.
  • Senior relief: Wyomingites 65 or older who have paid Wyoming property tax for at least 25 years receive a 50 percent cut.

Refund applications are made at wptrs.wyo.gov. The 2025 Legislature added $10.5 million to the refund program, so call the state office for the current round and its dates.

sections.h2: Valuation date and how to appeal your assessment
sections.html:
Wyoming property is listed, valued and assessed as of January 1, and an appeal begins with the county assessor. Laramie County mails assessment schedules no later than the fourth Monday in April, and written objections must reach the assessor within 30 days of the mailing date.

The county board of equalization decides current-year protests in writing by October 1. Under W.S. 39-13-109(b)(i) it can affirm the assessor or find for the taxpayer. Further appeals go to the State Board of Equalization and then to district court.

An appeal has to address market value, not the tax rate, and must include evidence supporting your estimate. If you are about to sell, useful evidence includes a recent appraisal, photos of defects the assessor may not have seen, and any signed purchase contract showing what a buyer will pay.

Tax is paid in two halves, and late balances accrue interest at 18 percent per year. Laramie County mails notices the last business day of August.

InstallmentDuePay by
First halfSeptember 1November 10
Second halfMarch 1May 10 of the next year

Paying the entire bill by December 31 waives the interest on the first half. The county treasurer certifies a delinquent list if taxes remain unpaid after May 11, and a demand notice goes out about five business days later. Unpaid taxes are still owed even if you never received the bill.

Many owners pay through a mortgage escrow account. In Laramie County, if both the lender and the owner pay, the treasurer keeps the first payment and refunds the duplicate. Before listing a house, ask the treasurer to confirm that the escrow payment posted.

sections.h2: What happens if Wyoming property tax goes unpaid?
sections.html:
Unpaid real property tax becomes a perpetual lien on the property, and the county can sell it at a tax sale. Under W.S. 39-13-108, the lien ranks ahead of all persons except the United States and the State of Wyoming.

  • The treasurer advertises the sale once a week for three weeks in a legal newspaper, with the first notice at least four weeks before the sale.
  • Sales take place at the county courthouse between 9:00 a.m. and 5:00 p.m., excluding Sundays.
  • The buyer who pays the taxes, interest, penalties and costs receives a certificate of purchase.
  • If the property does not sell for the amount owed, the county treasurer bids it in for the county.
  • A tax deed can issue for unredeemed property four years after the sale, after notice to occupants, owners and mortgagees at least three months beforehand.

Procedures change, so ask the treasurer for current details. The sooner you resolve a delinquency, the more options you keep.

sections.h2: Handling property tax when you sell
sections.html:
The simplest approach is to get a payoff figure from the county treasurer and have it paid from sale proceeds at closing. The tax is a lien on the real property, so it stays with the house until paid.

The deed is recorded with the county clerk along with a sworn statement from the grantee or the grantee's agent, as W.S. 34-1-142 requires. That statement discloses the price and terms but is kept confidential, and it may be shown only to someone reviewing or contesting a property tax assessment.

After a sale, the 25 percent exemption and any other exemption may not carry over. The exemption depends on the owner living in the house, so the buyer may have to file their own affidavit.

If you inherited the house or are selling after a death, the small estate limit rose to $400,000 on July 1, 2025. That can speed up transfer when real property is part of a modest estate.

A short checklist before listing: ask the treasurer for a payoff figure, confirm both halves are paid or scheduled, check that any escrow payment posted, and ask the assessor which exemptions are on file. A cash buyer can close around an open tax bill too, since the balance comes out of the proceeds like any other lien.

faqs.q: What percent of market value is Wyoming residential property assessed at?
faqs.a: Residential property is assessed at 9.5 percent of market value. Industrial property is 11.5 percent and minerals are 100 percent.

faqs.q: What is the Wyoming average mill levy?
faqs.a: The statewide average was 65.280 mills for the 2025 tax year. County averages ranged from 57.772 in Teton County to 73.826 in Big Horn County.

faqs.q: How do I qualify for the 25 percent homeowner exemption?
faqs.a: You must own and live in the home at least eight months of the year and file an affidavit with your county assessor. The exemption covers 25 percent of fair market value up to $1 million.

faqs.q: What interest does Wyoming charge on late property tax?
faqs.a: Delinquent balances accrue 18 percent interest per year. Paying the whole bill by December 31 waives interest on the first half.

faqs.q: Where do I appeal a Wyoming property assessment?
faqs.a: File with the county assessor within 30 days of the assessment schedule notice. The county board of equalization hears it and decides by October 1.
